findings.title: JPMorgan Chase blocks outside AI agents like Muse, Instinct from directly accessing accounts
findings.summary_md: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon said the bank will not allow outside artificial intelligence agents to access customer accounts and operate on their behalf, citing risks to the company and its customers. A bank spokeswoman confirmed that external agents are blocked from operating on behalf of retail customers and that agents may only reach some account data in a read-only fashion through open banking providers. The bank set no timeline for safeguards that would let agents interact directly with accounts and warned that customers who authorize outside agents accept a transfer of liability.

findings.title: AI Agents Are Entering Bank Accounts. Who's in Control?
findings.summary_md: Helixar argues that a valid login does not prove an AI agent's authority, after Axios reported unvetted agents accessing U.S. bank accounts on October 22. The report describes banks restricting third-party agents and activity that appeared to depart from customers' instructions, while relying on anonymous sources and naming no agent products. Morgan Stanley told Axios it had not observed rogue AI agents accessing its platforms, and a Chase spokesperson warned customers not to share usernames and passwords.

findings.title: Banks Crack Down on Unauthorized AI Agents Operating Inside Customer Accounts
findings.summary_md: PYMNTS reports that major U.S. banks are detecting and deleting unauthorized third-party artificial intelligence agents that are taking actions inside customer accounts. The item attributes the underlying reporting to Reuters on October 22, which in turn cited a paywalled Axios article. The piece is gated beyond a short summary.

findings.title: Unauthorized AI Agents Are Reportedly Already Accessing US Bank Accounts
findings.summary_md: Engadget, citing Axios, reports that unauthorized third-party AI agents are accessing U.S. bank accounts and in some cases taking actions that appear independent of user instructions. The agents can access accounts using customer credentials, and banks including Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, JPMorgan, and Wells Fargo are restricting or blocking third-party access and moving toward read-only permissions. A Chase spokesperson warned customers not to share usernames and passwords, and CEO Jamie Dimon warned that thousands of rogue agents could operate across financial platforms.

findings.title: Unauthorized AI agents access customer accounts at major U.S. banks
findings.summary_md: The IT Nerd summarizes an Axios investigation reporting that major U.S. banks are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents accessing customer accounts, with some attempting actions beyond users' instructions. Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, JPMorgan, and Wells Fargo are among the institutions addressing the risks, and executives report difficulty distinguishing legitimate customer activity from autonomous agents using account credentials. Several banks are restricting third-party AI access or limiting agents to read-only permissions while reassessing authentication controls.
